transcript.en: Around 10 years ago, Australia Zoo, the University of Queensland and Queensland Parks and Wildlife undertook a project to monitor the movements and behavior of the crocodiles in Lakefield National Park.
transcript.zh: 大约 10 年前，澳大利亚动物园、昆士兰大学和昆士兰公园与野生动物组织开展了一项监测莱克菲尔德国家公园鳄鱼活动和行为的项目。

transcript.en: The aim of the study was to provide better information on how adult crocodiles there interact within a river system, enabling people to have better decisions on how to manage crocodile populations.
transcript.zh: 该研究的目的是提供有关成年鳄鱼如何与河流系统相互作用的更全面信息，使人们能够更好地决定如何管理鳄鱼种群。

transcript.en: This project can lead the world in crocodile management because of the use of satellite, which enables scientists to stably receive accurate information being sent back to them on the computer.
transcript.zh: 这个项目在鳄鱼管理方面世界领先，因为使用了卫星，这使得科学家能够稳定地接收到计算机上发送回的准确信息。

transcript.en: Even though the crocodiles can travel very long distances, scientists can still know where they are, and study their habits.
transcript.zh: 尽管鳄鱼会游很远的距离，但科学家们仍然知道它们在哪里，并研究它们的习性。

transcript.en: The study is going to help scientists gain further knowledge on crocodile behavior, which can help make informed decisions on the management plans for crocodiles not only in Australia but around the world.
transcript.zh: 该研究将帮助科学家进一步了解鳄鱼的行为，这有助于不仅在澳大利亚，而且在世界各地就鳄鱼的管理计划做出可靠的决定。

transcript.en: Crocodile tracking isn’t a new idea in Australia.
transcript.zh: 鳄鱼追踪在澳大利亚并不是什么新鲜事。

transcript.en: Crocodile studies have been previously conducted by radio.
transcript.zh: 鳄鱼研究以前是通过无线电进行的。

transcript.en: A miniature electronic device was implanted under the skin of these animals and they were released back into the river.
transcript.zh: 将微型电子设备植入这些动物的皮肤下，然后将它们放回河中。

transcript.en: These tags enabled scientists to track the movements of these particular crocodiles over the next 10 years.
transcript.zh: 这些标签使科学家能够追踪这些鳄鱼在未来10年内的活动。

transcript.en: Of course, there are some unexpected challenges.
transcript.zh: 当然，也有一些意想不到的挑战。

transcript.en: The data transmitted from each receiver is recorded by some devices employed in the receiving stations.
transcript.zh: 从每个接收器中传输的数据由接收站中使用的一些设备记录下来。

transcript.en: However, some devices are too old that they always lose signals due to a variety of reasons.
transcript.zh: 但是，有些设备太旧了，由于各种原因，它们总是丢失信号。

transcript.en: So, they can’t track those animals which they have been studying for months.
transcript.zh: 所以，他们无法追踪他们研究了几个月的那些动物。

transcript.en: In order to study the crocodiles, they must first be captured so that the device can be put on them.
transcript.zh: 为了研究鳄鱼，必须先将它们捕获，以便将设备放在它们身上。

transcript.en: But this is a very difficult task because they are alert and afraid of being followed by humans.
transcript.zh: 但这是一项非常艰巨的任务，因为它们很警觉，害怕被人类追踪。

transcript.en: So it might take the team several hours to capture one.
transcript.zh: 所以团队可能需要几个小时才能捕获一个。

transcript.en: The tracking device has signal transmitters inside and it’s waterproof.
transcript.zh: 追踪器内部有防水的信号发射器。

transcript.en: It is attached to the head of the crocodile, so the crocodile cannot remove the device with its feet or tail.
transcript.zh: 它附在鳄鱼的头上，所以鳄鱼不能用它的脚或尾巴取下这个装置。

transcript.en: The research has begun to reveal the movements of crocodiles.
transcript.zh: 研究已经开始展示鳄鱼的活动了。

transcript.en: Data showed that crocodiles tend to be more active at night time.
transcript.zh: 数据显示鳄鱼往往在夜间更活跃。

transcript.en: The GPS sometimes shows that in some areas the crocodiles are overpopulated, so scientists at the park have to use a helicopter to relocate the crocodiles in order to control their population in the area.
transcript.zh: 全球卫星定位系统有时会显示某些地区的鳄鱼数量过多，因此公园的科学家不得不使用直升机重新安置鳄鱼，以控制该地区的鳄鱼数量。

transcript.en: A crocodile would be taken many kilometers away from its original place.
transcript.zh: 一条鳄鱼会被带到离它原来的地方很多公里远的地方。

transcript.en: However, scientists found that the relocation methods were ineffective because the relocated crocodiles will return to their original location following the most direct route within one week.
transcript.zh: 然而，科学家们发现，重新安置的方法是无效的，因为被带离的鳄鱼会在一周内沿着最直接的路线回到原来的位置。

transcript.en: The tracking data shows that the crocodiles swim right back to where they came from when moved.
transcript.zh: 追踪数据显示，鳄鱼直接游回原处。

transcript.en: Crocodiles sometimes travel hundreds of kilometers from Indonesia to Australia in order to reproduce.
transcript.zh: 鳄鱼有时会从印度尼西亚到澳大利亚移动数百公里以进行繁殖。

transcript.en: It is interesting to see that they can always find their way and they will not get lost in the ocean.
transcript.zh: 有趣的是，它们总能找到自己的路，不会迷失在大海中。

transcript.en: Scientists realized the crocodiles are able to navigate.
transcript.zh: 科学家们意识到鳄鱼能够导航。

transcript.en: This is an important ability for them when they have to migrate for very long distances.
transcript.zh: 当它们必须迁徙很长的距离时，这对它们来说是一项重要的能力。

transcript.en: We may wonder if human beings can learn from the crocodiles and find our way without using technology.
transcript.zh: 我们可能想知道人类是否可以向鳄鱼学习在不使用技术的情况下找回自己的路。

transcript.en: However, through lots of research and experiments, scientists conclude that crocodiles can tell directions by using their senses to the sun, so that they know where they’re going.
transcript.zh: 然而，通过大量的研究和实验，科学家们得出结论，鳄鱼可以通过对太阳的感知来判断方向，从而知道自己要去哪里。

transcript.en: This is an ability which human beings don’t possess.
transcript.zh: 这是人类不具备的能力。

transcript.en: Another finding is that, like the migration of birds who can travel thousands and thousands of kilometers, crocodiles have the same system to help them travel.
transcript.zh: 另一个发现是，就像鸟类可以迁徙数千公里一样，鳄鱼也有相同的系统来帮助它们迁徙。

transcript.en: The research is still going on in northern Australia.
transcript.zh: 这项研究在澳大利亚北部仍在进行。

transcript.en: Scientists are working hard to gather more information about this amazing creature.
transcript.zh: 科学家们正在努力收集有关这种神奇生物的更多信息。
